definitions.explanation: A Japanese festival held on March 3 to pray for the health and happiness of girls. Families display ornamental dolls and celebrate with special foods.

examples.japanese: ひな{祭|まつ}りは{三月三日|さんがつみっか}だ。
ひな{祭|まつ}りにひな{人形|にんぎょう}を{飾|かざ}った。
examples.english: We displayed the hina dolls for Girls' Day.

examples.japanese: ひな{祭|まつ}りが{終|お}わったらすぐにひな{人形|にんぎょう}を{片付|かたづ}けないと、{嫁|よめ}に{行|い}き{遅|おく}れると{言|い}われている。
examples.english: It's said that if you don't put away the hina dolls right after Girls' Day, the girl will be late to marry.

notes:
WRITING:
Also written as {雛祭|ひなまつ}り or {雛|ひな}{祭|まつ}り. The kanji {雛|ひな} means "chick" or "small doll."

CULTURAL NOTE:
Also known as {桃|もも}の{節句|せっく} (Peach Blossom Festival). Families with daughters display a set of ornamental dolls ({雛|ひな}{人形|にんぎょう}) representing the Emperor, Empress, and their court on a tiered platform. Traditional foods include ちらし{寿司|ずし}, {菱餅|ひしもち} (diamond-shaped rice cakes), ひなあられ (sweet rice crackers), and {白酒|しろざけ} (sweet white sake).

SUPERSTITION:
It is widely believed that leaving the dolls out after March 3 will delay the daughter's marriage.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ひな{人形|にんぎょう}: hina dolls
- ひな{祭|まつ}りの{歌|うた}: the Girls' Day song
